accuracy.evidence: Checked against the KS3 programme of study (DfE 2013: properties of metals and non-metals; acidity of metal and non-metal oxides), RSC Education practical notes and RSC periodic table data: copper, aluminium, iron and nickel conduct and are malleable; sulfur and iodine are brittle insulators; graphite conducts while diamond does not; mercury is liquid and sodium soft; only iron, nickel, cobalt and steel are attracted to a magnet; magnesium oxide (about pH 10) and sodium oxide (about pH 14) are basic, carbon dioxide (about pH 5.6) and sulfur dioxide (about pH 3) acidic, with universal indicator colours on the standard chart. The staircase is drawn left of B, Si and As, with B, Si, Ge and As shaded as metalloids, and hydrogen is classed a non-metal.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS3 slips: only metals conduct (graphite prediction in the circuit step, tag conduct), all metals are magnetic (magnet prediction, copper and aluminium cards, tag magnet), shine means metal (iodine card in the evidence sort, tag shiny), every metal is a hard solid (mercury and sodium cards, tag solid), hydrogen is a metal because it sits above group 1 (staircase prediction, tag left) and metal oxides are acids (oxide prediction, tag oxide).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmetnon is built on this topic's own evidence: a circuit with a gap that lights for metals and graphite, an anvil that flattens metals and shatters or crumbles non-metals, a magnet that pulls only iron and nickel, an evidence sort of misleading elements, a compressed periodic table with the metal and non-metal staircase, and a universal indicator beaker for oxides. It is not the group trends lab or the alkali metals lab. Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Pupils discover each rule from their own tests before the text states it: the bulb lights for graphite, the magnet ignores copper and aluminium, the hammer flattens metals and shatters sulfur and iodine, and the indicator turns blue or purple for metal oxides and red or orange for non-metal oxides. The evidence sort then forces several properties to be weighed together, which is the key idea; each done line confirms in one sentence.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'No, only metals conduct' (graphite lights the bulb), 'Yes, all metals are magnetic' (copper and aluminium show no pull), 'Yes, it is on the left' for hydrogen (the staircase step classes H a non-metal with its reason), and 'Red: acidic' for magnesium oxide (the beaker turns blue at pH 10). The done message reveals the locked-in prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions; every wrong option is tagged to a named slip with its own message: shiny (iodine is shiny but brittle and an insulator), conduct (graphite), magnet (only iron, nickel, cobalt and steel), solid (mercury), left (hydrogen) and oxide (metal oxides make alkalis). In-step feedback in the sort and table steps also names the element and the reason, e.g. 'Bromine is in group 7, right of the staircase. It is a non-metal, even though it is a liquid.'

readability.evidence: Kid text for 11 to 13 year olds uses short sentences and defines each term as it appears (malleable, insulator), reading at about FK grade 4.7; adult text was rewritten to about FK grade 9.1, inside the validator's limit. Canvas labels are element symbols plus one-word names at 13 to 19 px, and every result is also spoken in the live region.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no filler phrases, under 12% six-word overlap with any other lesson). Each kid paragraph teaches one point (metal properties, non-metal properties, why one test is not enough, the periodic table and oxides); adult paragraphs give the curriculum link and vocabulary, the exceptions, named mistakes and a lab summary.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the 5 sample tiles fit one row at about 66 px wide with symbol, name and result, the test station fills the space above, the periodic table fits 9 columns of about 38 px with readable symbols, the Metal and Non-metal boxes are half width each, and the 4 oxide tiles fit one row under the beaker. Buttons under the canvas wrap; nothing is clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: 'Test copper' for each untested sample, Metal and Non-metal labelled with the element ('Magnesium is a metal', 'K is a metal'), and 'Add magnesium oxide' for each oxide. note() updates the canvas aria-label and the polite live region with the result after every test; the walk gate's axe run is clean (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
